sociability.text: let an old friend's message sit until answering it would have been strange
turned down the neighbor's offer and closed the door before they finished asking
slipped out the side door while the others were still stacking chairs
stayed in the car until the lobby had emptied of familiar voices
cancelled the standing coffee date and sent nothing in its place
looked down at their keys until the familiar face had passed the window
watched the friends arrive from the upstairs window and did not come down
chose the self-checkout to skip the usual few words with the cashier
let the conversation with an old friend die after two replies
set the table for one though their sister had said she might stop by
spread a bag across the next bus seat so nobody would take it
ate lunch on the landing between floors rather than at the table with the others
left the family dinner before the dishes reached the sink
skipped a friend's birthday lunch and did not bother to make up a reason
chose the cafeteria seat farthest from the usual table
heard the laughter next door through the wall and turned the television up
said "we should get together" to a neighbor and meant the opposite
took the longer route home to avoid the bench where the regulars sit
read the invitation, pictured the small talk, and let the date go by
stopped going to the weekly thing and waited to see who would notice
sat out the game at recess and told the teacher they were tired

warmth.text: said the sharp thing to their sister and let it stand
laughed when their brother tripped on the curb and dropped everything

enjoyed watching the neighbor's new plant wilt inside a week
felt glad when the kid across the hall got scolded on the landing

heard a friend's good news and found the flaw in it out loud
did not ask how the appointment went, though they remembered the day
withheld the toy until the other kid stopped asking
answered their kid's question with the shortest reply that would end it
decided a friend's apology was not enough and said so
kept the better headphones for the long part of the ride

put the book they meant to finish back on the shelf with the marker still in it

left the gym bag by the door for the second week
did the job well enough that nobody would say anything and no better
let someone else volunteer and studied the table until it was settled

put the unfamiliar spice back on the shelf and reached for the old jar
shut the recipe book at the first unfamiliar step and opened the drawer of takeout menus
told their sister the book club pick would disappoint and named an author they already liked
laughed at their kid's wish to plant something new and handed over the old rake
told an old friend the new shoes would hurt and laced up the broken-in pair
kept describing how the storefront used to look while the neighbor pointed at what it was now

let the other person believe the error had been theirs from the start

kept quiet when the wrong person was blamed for the noise
let their kid believe the toy had simply disappeared from the shelf

hid the homework note and said the teacher had not handed any out

let their parent think the mess in the kitchen was someone else's

ate dinner standing in the kitchen instead of at the table with the others

skipped the Saturday market and stayed in to sort old mail
kept the coat on the hook and ate dinner in the same chair as lunch
